elbow_flex.source: fitnessprogramer One-Arm Triceps Pushdown: "Lower the handle until your arm is fully extended but not locked out" (illustrative 10 degrees); no source gives an exact starting angle, so the bent start is illustrative at 90 degrees, matching the elbow-at-the-side start ACE describes for the two-arm version

shoulder_flex.source: ACE Triceps Pushdowns: "Your elbows are aligned with the mid-point of your trunk, arms positioned firmly by sides" for the whole rep

torso_lean.source: Gravitus Pushdown: warns against "leaning back or using momentum" when the weight is too heavy, i.e. stand upright with minimal lean

muscles.peakSource: fitnessprogramer One-Arm Triceps Pushdown: the rep works toward "fully extended but not locked out," so triceps effort is highest approaching that near-extended bottom

mistake.name: Flare and lean

tells.text: The elbow drifts forward off the ribs instead of staying pinned.
The torso leans into it, using body weight to help push down.

mistake.source: Gravitus Pushdown: "Allowing elbows to flare away from your sides turns this isolation exercise into a less effective movement"; leaning back or using momentum on a too-heavy weight compromises the form the same way

sources: Contact fact (D-FG7 (e), the single-arm id): a single D-handle at the high pulley, one hand (fitnessprogramer One-Arm Triceps Pushdown)
